title: When Good Intentions Go Wrong
field_courseInformation: Most leadership missteps don’t come from bad decisions. They come from good ones made with the best intentions. So why do they still go wrong? Well-meaning actions can create unintended consequences, so leaders need to ensure their decisions truly support their teams.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define the difference between leadership intent and leadership impact.
  • Explain why positive motives can still produce negative organizational outcomes.
  • Identify common leadership behaviors that begin with good intentions but create unintended harm.
  • Analyze workplace scenarios to distinguish between intent and impact.
  • Apply practical strategies to test assumptions, seek feedback, and adjust behavior to reduce unintended consequences.
field_courseOutline:

  • How to Avoid the Pitfalls

field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define how cultural differences influence communication styles in workplace conversations.
  • Explain how AI can be used as a preparation tool for cross-cultural interactions.
  • Apply structured prompts to simulate culturally specific responses using AI.
  • Analyze potential communication risks or misunderstandings using AI-generated insights.
  • Practice adapting messaging and tone for different cultural contexts using AI feedback.

title: From Compliance to Engagement: Supporting Frontline Safety Leaders
field_courseInformation: Strong safety cultures depend on more than rules and compliance. Managers and supervisors strengthen safety performance when they empower frontline employees to participate, communicate concerns, and take ownership of safety initiatives. This ultimately builds trust, encourages reporting, and creates shared accountability.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Explore how to build and sustain a strong safety culture by empowering frontline employees to take ownership of safety practices.

  • Create open, two-way communication channels-such as town halls, open-door policies, and anonymous reporting systems-that enable upward feedback from frontline workers.
  • Delegate roles and responsibilities to employees who can begin playing a role in your safety program.
  • Implement methods to recognize and reward employee-led safety initiatives and decisions that promote accountability and continuous improvement.

title: Confined Spaces: Personnel, Permits, and Protection (UK)
field_courseInformation: A confined space isn't defined by its size — it's defined by its hazards, and the responsibilities that come with entering one are equally serious. UK regulations require clearly defined roles, documented safe systems of work, and PPE selection matched to specific risks before any entry begins. Supervisors and workers who understand what each role demands, what a permit must contain, and how to maintain their equipment are the ones who catch problems before they become emergencies.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define a "confined space" and what causes a confined space to require a permit, using HSE criteria.
  • Differentiate roles such as Authorized Entrant, Attendant, and Entry Supervisor, and explain their responsibilities that must be carried out if entry is required.
  • Interpret the essential elements of a permit (entry procedures, authorized entrants, prerequisites). Understand permit-to-work systems and the essential elements needed.
  • Develop or assess a written confined space program consistent with regulatory requirements.
  • Identify appropriate PPE and RPE based on hazard scenarios, as well as proper storage and maintenance procedures.
  • Recommend documentation, training timing, and recordkeeping practices aligned with HSE standards.

title: Confined Spaces: Emergency and Rescue Procedures (UK)
field_courseInformation: Confined space emergencies can turn fatal within minutes, and survival often depends on decisions made long before anyone steps inside. Under UK law, suitable emergency arrangements must be in place before any confined space entry — and those arrangements must be specific, tested, and ready. Workers and supervisors who understand rescue methods, role assignments, and documentation requirements are better positioned to act decisively when seconds matter.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Explain why timely rescue planning matters, including fatality rates risks and rescuer hazards.
  • Differentiate between nonentry and entry rescue methods, with pros/cons and prerequisites.
  • Assign roles and duties, and coordinate with external responders.
  • Construct a documented emergency rescue plan for confined space incidents, including communication flows, first aid, hazard awareness, and local authority involvement.
  • Plan and execute practice drills and post-incident review protocols.

title: Confined Spaces: Identifying Hazards (UK)
field_courseInformation: In confined spaces, hazards don't announce themselves — oxygen levels can drop, toxic gases can accumulate, and physical dangers can combine without warning before anyone realizes conditions have changed. UK regulations require a suitable and sufficient risk assessment before work begins, and that assessment depends on knowing exactly what to look for and how to find it. Workers and supervisors who can identify atmospheric and non-atmospheric hazards, interpret monitoring data, and apply the right controls are the ones who make it home.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify common atmospheric hazards (oxygen deficiency and enrichment, flammable gases, toxic gases) and non-atmospheric hazards in confined spaces.
  • Explain the standard order and methods for atmospheric testing (oxygen → flammables → toxic → others).
  • Differentiate between continuous and periodic monitoring strategies and interpret results versus permissible limits.
  • Determine the hierarchy of controls (eliminate, substitute, engineering, administrative, PPE) for hazard mitigation.
  • Develop or refine hazard communication strategies (signage, labeling, pre-entry alerts).

title: Working at Height: Rescue During Work at Height (UK)
field_courseInformation: Rescue planning is a critical part of working at height. Effective rescue procedures, trained personnel, appropriate equipment, and clear communication help organizations respond quickly when emergencies occur and reduce the risk of serious injury or fatality.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Understand the fundamental requirements of the Work at Height Regulations 2005 (WAHR) and recognise what constitutes work at height, including common risk scenarios in UK workplaces.
  • Apply the hierarchy of controls-avoid, prevent, minimise-to real-world tasks by selecting appropriate protective measures, equipment, and procedures for safe work at height.
  • Analyse work environments and tasks to identify hazards such as fragile surfaces, weather conditions, unsafe equipment, or poor planning, and determine suitable collective and personal protection systems.
  • Evaluate the competence of workers, adequacy of equipment, and effectiveness of safety plans to ensure regulatory compliance and continuous risk reduction.
  • Demonstrate informed decision-making in reporting hazards, following safe systems of work, and contributing to employer-employee collaboration on health and safety planning.

field_courseInformation: Asbestos remains present in many UK buildings constructed before 2000, and disturbing it without proper precautions can cause irreversible, life-threatening illness. Workers across industries face exposure risk during maintenance, renovation, and demolition tasks on older structures. Understanding how to identify asbestos-containing materials, comply with UK legal requirements, and apply the right controls protects workers and keeps employers on the right side of the law.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define what asbestos is and identify where it is commonly found in UK buildings.
  • Explain the health risks associated with asbestos exposure, including long-term diseases.
  • Recognise common asbestos-containing materials (ACMs) in UK workplaces.
  • Apply appropriate actions when asbestos is suspected or disturbed, following UK regulations.
  • Identify key control measures and employer/employee responsibilities under UK asbestos safety laws.

title: The Witness's Role in Harassment Prevention (Canada)
field_courseInformation: Empower yourself to create a safer, more respectful workplace by learning the critical role of witness intervention. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of harassment, discrimination, and workplace violence under Canadian federal and provincial law, then equips you with actionable strategies to recognize and address these issues as an active witness. Through the "4 D's of Intervention" framework and real-world scenarios, you'll gain the confidence to overcome barriers to action, intervene effectively and safely, support colleagues, and foster a culture of upstanders. Because creating a respectful workplace isn't just about knowing the law — it's about taking responsibility to act when it matters.
field_courseRegulations:
• ARLS / Bill 42 — Complaint and reporting procedures are required policy components; witness obligations support the required complaint-handling framework
  • Canada Labour Code Part II / SOR/2020-130 — Reporting obligations and bystander responsibilities are explicitly required components of federal harassment prevention training
  • OHS Act (PEI) / Harassment Prevention Regulations — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • OHS Act / General Regulation 91-191 — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • OHS Act / Workplace Harassment Regulations — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • OHS Act, 2022 — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • OHS Code Part 27 (ss.390-392) — Workers must be trained on how to report harassment; witness/bystander reporting supports the required prevention plan
  • OHSA ss.32.0.1–32.0.7 — Training must cover how to report incidents including when the supervisor is the alleged harasser; witness obligations included
  • Saskatchewan Employment Act / s.3-25 — Workers must be trained on reporting; General Duty (s.3-8) supports broad safety training obligations
  • Workers Compensation Act / WorkSafeBC Policy P2-21-2 — Reporting and response obligations are required training content
  • Workers' Safety and Compensation Act / OHS Regulations Part 19 — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • Workplace Safety and Health Act / Man. Reg. 82/2011 — Reporting procedures are required training content
  • WSCC / Safety Act — Reporting procedures are required training content

title: The Manager's Role in Harassment Prevention and the Respectful Workplace (Canada)
field_courseInformation: This course empowers managers and supervisors to identify, prevent, and address harassment and workplace violence effectively. You'll gain a comprehensive understanding of your legal duties under Canadian federal and provincial legislation, then learn to go from compliance to culture-shift. Through real-world scenarios involving microaggressions, disrespectful behaviors, and serious safety concerns, you'll gain actionable strategies to respond to reports, conduct fair investigations, support affected workers, and model respectful leadership. Learn to recognize early warning signs, mitigate risks, enforce policies consistently, and create a psychologically safe environment where your team feels secure, valued, and empowered to speak up.
field_courseRegulations:

  • OHS Act (PEI) / Harassment Prevention Regulations - Managers trained as part of all-employee requirement

  • OHS Act / Workplace Harassment Regulations - Supervisors receive additional content on their specific responsibilities
  • OHS Act, 2022 - Managers trained as part of all-employee requirement

field_courseInformation: Employee discontent often appears through quiet shifts in energy, participation, initiative, or trust before performance visibly declines. Leaders who notice these patterns early, ask better questions, and follow through consistently can address concerns before dissatisfaction becomes disengagement.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define the factors contributing to employee discontent and distinguish between transient dissatisfaction and systemic workplace issues.
  • Identify early warning signs of employee unhappiness within their teams.
  • Analyze the impact of economic uncertainty and AI concerns on employee motivation and engagement.
  • Reflect on their current leadership practices to detect gaps in support and communication.
  • Apply specific strategies to address employee discontent in ways that reinforce trust and organizational goals.
  • Design a plan for ongoing engagement and follow-up that helps sustain positive workplace experiences.
field_courseOutline:
• Understanding Employee Discontent
  • Early Warning Signs
  • Leadership Self-Reflection
  • Practical Strategies That Rebuild Engagement
  • Sustaining Engagement Over Time

title: The Hidden Risk of Cognitive Overload
field_courseInformation: Cognitive overload isn’t a motivation problem or a focus problem — it’s a structural one. Managers and employees who understand how mental capacity works can spot the real cause behind missed details, slower decisions, and team disengagement. Targeted habit changes, applied consistently, restore clarity and sustain performance without requiring anyone to work less.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define cognitive overload and explain how it impacts focus, decision-making, productivity and wellness in the workplace.
  • Identify the three types of cognitive load (intrinsic, extraneous, germane) and explain how each plays out in everyday work contexts.
  • Determine common causes of cognitive overload at work and identify the signs that you or a team member is dealing with cognitive overload.
  • Develop practices for yourself, or to support team members, for reducing cognitive load.
field_courseOutline:
• What Is Cognitive Overload?
  • 3 Types of Cognitive Overload
  • Signs of Overload
  • How To Reduce the Extraneous Load

  • Respond to problems with PPE by reporting issues.

title: 301-18-UKEU Regulatory Overview and Electrical Safety Equipment
field_courseInformation: This lesson describes how appropriate regulatory agencies divide electrical safety jurisdiction among physical plant, work practices, and public settings. These agencies administer strict rules and regulations for the safeguard of employers, employees, and the public. The basic electrical principles used by these regulatory agencies to develop safe working environments and work procedures are discussed in this lesson. The lesson also explains how substation ground grids, multi-grounded neutrals (MGN) on distribution lines, shield wires on transmission lines, and grounding electrodes on other electrical facilities provide great benefits to system operations and personnel safety. It covers how they are designed, installed, and used to provide electrical safety during system faults, lightning strikes, and other overvoltage conditions. Also discussed are common ground grid safety enhancements, such as gravel, switching platforms, equipment bonding, and more.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Discuss the regulatory agencies that are directly involved in assuring electrically safe environments for employers, employees, and public
  • Describe the fundamental electrical principles used by regulatory agencies in their pursuit to ensure safe working environments and to avoid accidental injury accidents
  • Describe how substations and other electrical facilities are grounded to earth for the safety of personnel
  • Explain how substation ground grids and other grounding schemes are designed, installed, and tested
  • Describe how power faults occur
  • Describe the various types of faults that occur on distribution systems
  • Describe how fault current distributes throughout grounding locations
  • Explain where to expect hazardous potentials to appear

title: Stress Management: Handling and Managing Stress (UK)
field_courseInformation: Stress can build quickly when early warning signs go unnoticed, but simple coping strategies can make pressure easier to manage. Techniques like self-compassion, positive self-talk, physical activity, and reframing can help calm the body and shift perspective. Resilience also grows through daily routines that support sleep, healthy habits, social connection, and realistic expectations. Planning tasks with clear times and places can make stress prevention feel more practical and achievable.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify early signs of stress and opportunities for intervention.
  • Apply practical stress-reduction techniques such as self-compassion, positive self-talk, and relaxation strategies.
  • Use mindfulness and physical activity to reduce stress reactions.
  • Reframe stressful situations to build resilience.
  • Develop preventive routines including sleep (7-9 hours), planning habits, and social connection.
field_courseOutline:
• Managing and Reducing Stress
  • The Road to Resilience
  • Prioritizing Stress Prevention

title: Stress Management: Avoidable and Unavoidable Stress (UK)
field_courseInformation: Some stress comes from situations people can influence, such as unclear expectations, poor planning, or ineffective communication. Other stress comes from circumstances outside one person’s control, including organisational change, economic pressure, or unexpected demands. Recognising the difference helps people focus their energy where it can make the greatest impact. Practical habits like clarifying priorities, tracking stress signals, practising self-care, and seeking support can reduce strain and improve resilience.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Differentiate between avoidable and unavoidable stressors.
  • Identify common workplace sources of avoidable stress, including time management and unclear expectations.
  • Explain unavoidable organisational stressors such as restructuring or economic shifts.
  • Describe the short- and long-term health effects of stress.
  • Apply practical strategies to reduce avoidable stress and cope with unavoidable stress.
field_courseOutline:
• Workplace Stress Sources

title: Stress Management: Understanding Stress and Burnout (UK)
field_courseInformation: Stress can affect the mind, body, emotions, and daily habits long before it becomes overwhelming. Early signs like fatigue, racing thoughts, irritability, sleep disruption, or withdrawal can reveal when it has started to take a toll. Burnout develops when stress continues without enough recovery, support, or healthy coping strategies. Discover how small, consistent actions like setting boundaries, taking breaks, and reaching out to others for support can help protect well-being before stress becomes harder to manage.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define stress using a single, comprehensive description aligned with UK health guidance.
  • Identify physical, psychological, emotional, and behavioural symptoms of stress.
  • Distinguish between manageable stress and burnout caused by prolonged stress exposure.
  • Recognize common causes and effects of stress across work, home, and life events.
  • Explain how chronic stress leads to burnout and its impacts on wellbeing.
field_courseOutline:

  • Stress VS. Burnout

title: How To Use AI for Brainstorming and Problem Solving
field_courseInformation: Stalled ideas can slow down projects like campaign planning, workshop design, or solving team challenges under pressure. AI supports brainstorming by generating diverse directions, organizing thinking into structured outputs, and helping refine rough ideas into usable plans. With clear prompts and iterative adjustments, it becomes easier to move from a blank page to a prioritized strategy or actionable concept.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define how AI can support and enhance brainstorming and problem-solving activities in a work context.
  • Craft clear AI prompts that generate diverse and relevant ideas for a given brainstorming challenge.
  • Refine AI outputs through iterative prompt adjustments to improve idea quality and relevance.
  • Apply AI-generated ideas within real work tasks such as strategy planning, decision framing, or creative concept development.
field_courseOutline:
• Ask
  • Adjust
  • Apply

title: How To Get Advice From AI
field_courseInformation: Learning how to use AI advice, AI decision making, and AI tools for work effectively can transform how modern employees approach complex decisions and problem solving. In this course, the learner explores structured and conversational methods for interacting with AI, including techniques like mental models, decision matrices, and structured frameworks that support clearer thinking and better outcomes. Through practical workplace scenarios, the learner will practice how to challenge AI outputs, reduce bias, and refine responses to ensure critical thinking with AI remains central to every interaction. Designed for professionals across industries, this training emphasizes real world application, helping the learner confidently integrate AI workplace productivity strategies into daily workflows while collaborating with human colleagues. By the end, the learner will be equipped to evaluate, adapt, and responsibly apply AI generated insights to support smarter, more informed decisions.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Use AI to get advice conversationally, in an informal framework, or in a formal framework.
  • Challenge the AI and help to eliminate bias.
  • Analyze the AI's advice and enact it in collaboration with their own judgment and human colleagues.

title: 531-01 Combustion Theory - Spanish
field_courseInformation: Energy is stored in fuel. That energy is released when the fuel is burned. Knowing basic combustion theory is necessary to understand how fuel is safely and efficiently used to generate electricity. The Combustion Theory training course explains the different types of fossil fuels used in an industrial setting and describes their characteristics. It also covers the elements and conditions that must be present for fuel combustion to happen. This course examines fossil fuels, fossil fuel characteristics, basic combustion process, combustion types, and the three T's of combustion. Combustion Theory is part of the Hydrocarbon Fired Boilers training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Describir la composición química básica de los combustibles fósiles
  • Definir los siguientes términos en lo que se refiere a la combustión: Energía química, Hidrocarburos
  • Explicar cómo los elementos del triángulo del fuego, junto con una reacción química sostenida, liberan energía a partir de los combustibles fósiles
  • Describir la diferencia entre el punto de inflamación y el punto de ignición
  • Explicar por qué las centrales eléctricas se fijan como objetivo la combustión completa
  • Analizar la relación entre el exceso de aire y las pruebas de oxígeno en la combustión de combustibles fósiles para la generación de energía
  • Indicar las tres T de la combustión

field_courseInformation: All operating machines produce vibration, but identifying when vibration signals a problem is essential for maintaining safe and reliable equipment. In this lesson, learners explore practical techniques for investigating vibration issues, including reviewing preliminary data, performing inspections, and distinguishing root causes from symptoms. Realistic examples and structured approaches, such as root cause analysis and guided inspection practices, reinforce key concepts. The lesson also highlights effective communication and consistent data collection methods to support accurate diagnosis. Designed for maintenance technicians, this training strengthens the ability to troubleshoot vibration problems and improve equipment performance.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Discuss how to examine preliminary vibration problem data and findings
  • List common machine vibration data collection points
  • Explain how to inspect a machine when investigating vibration problems
  • Identify the steps, procedures, and communication techniques employed in successful vibration troubleshooting
  • Differentiate between vibration problem symptoms and root causes

field_courseInformation: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) is a safety system used to control hazardous energy so equipment cannot start, move, or release stored power while work is being performed. Understanding what LOTO actually involves helps you recognise energy sources that are easy to overlook, including compressed air, hydraulic pressure, springs, and stored electrical charge. When these controls are applied correctly, everyday maintenance tasks become safer, more predictable, and far less likely to result in serious injury.

title: Portable Fire Extinguisher Safety (UK)
field_courseInformation: Fire emergencies can develop rapidly in any workplace, and understanding how to respond safely is essential for every employee. In this course, the learner explores UK fire classifications, extinguisher colour coding under BS EN 3, and the practical application of the PASS technique to tackle small, controllable fires. Realistic workplace scenarios demonstrate how to assess fire risks, identify the correct extinguisher type, and decide when evacuation is the safest option. Designed for a general UK audience seeking to strengthen fire safety knowledge, the training reinforces safe decision-making, legal awareness, and responsible action during an emergency.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Recognise Workplace Fire Hazards and Extinguisher Types
  • Identify common workplace fire hazards.
  • Understand UK fire classifications (A, B, C, D, and Electrical).
  • Match the appropriate fire extinguisher type (water, foam, CO₂, dry powder, wet chemical) to each classification.
  • Demonstrate Proper Fire Extinguisher Use
  • Apply the PASS (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep) technique in line with UK fire safety guidance.
  • Operate a fire extinguisher safely and effectively during a small, controllable fire.
  • Apply Workplace Fire Safety Procedures and Emergency Protocols
  • Understand organisational fire safety arrangements and responsibilities.
  • Know when to use a fire extinguisher and when to evacuate.
  • Follow procedures for raising the alarm and implementing the emergency plan in compliance with the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.
  • Assess Fire Situations Before Acting
  • Evaluate the size and location of the fire and smoke conditions.
  • Confirm safe access to an exit before attempting to fight a fire.
  • Determine whether it is safer to use an extinguisher or evacuate, based on the fire risk assessment and workplace procedures.
field_courseOutline:
• Elements and Classes of Fire
  • Fire Extinguisher Anatomy
  • Responding to a Fire
  • Pass Technique

field_courseInformation: AI-generated content can look polished while lacking accuracy, specificity, or real value. Recognizing these gaps helps you avoid sending vague reports, unsupported claims, or off-brand messaging to clients or colleagues. Clear prompting, careful review, and deliberate editing allow you to turn rough AI output into credible emails, summaries, and deliverables that reflect your expertise.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define "AI slop" and identify common warning signs in text and image outputs.
  • Explain why generative AI produces vague, inaccurate, or generic results.
  • Analyze AI output for clarity, credibility, tone, and usefulness before using it.
  • Determine when to refine the request versus when to rely on their own expertise and judgment.
  • Apply human skills-editing, fact-checking, contextual awareness, and creativity-to improve or replace weak AI output.

title: Human Skills You Need in the AI Era
field_courseInformation: AI is reshaping daily work, including drafting emails, summarizing information, and turning data into faster decisions. In this course, the learner examines how AI supports productivity while human skills protect quality, trust, and outcomes. The learner practices applying context, lived experience, and sound judgment to evaluate AI output, then refines workplace communication to reflect empathy and organizational culture. Practical examples reinforce ethical and strategic thinking so employees use AI with confidence and resilience in real workplace moments.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Contextual understanding - bringing situational awareness, cultural insight, and real-world perspective that helps interpret information accurately.
  • Empathy - sensing emotions, responding with care, and building trust in ways AI cannot genuinely replicate.
  • Strategic thinking - envisioning long-term goals, weighing trade-offs, and making decisions with organizational impact in mind.

  • Applying lived experience - using personal history, intuition, and wisdom to make informed, experience-based decisions.

title: AI Literacy: Iterating and Refining AI Output
field_courseInformation: Effective AI use depends on more than writing a single prompt. title: 350-05-UKEU Line Protection
field_courseInformation: Transmission, sub-transmission and distribution systems all have different operating characteristics and objectives. The way they transport power varies significantly; with each variation comes practical solutions to ensure safe and reliable operation. Each solution also has its limitations.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Explain the purpose of transmission relay loadability and why settings must balance security and dependability
  • Summarize how the Grid Code and ENTSO-E guidelines ensure relay settings support secure transmission capacity
  • Describe how overcurrent protection is coordinated on radial and interconnected systems
  • Explain how distribution networks use reclosers and sectionalisers, and how these are coordinated with upstream protection
  • Identify the strengths and limitations of overcurrent protection relays
  • Identify the strengths and limitations of distance protection
  • Explain how earth fault relay settings differ between distribution (impedance-earthed) and transmission (solidly-earthed) systems
  • Describe how mutual coupling between adjacent lines can lead to false tripping and how this can be mitigated
  • Define overlapping zones of protection and their role in ensuring complete coverage
  • Identify methods used to protect against voltage instability, including reactive power support and under-voltage load shedding
  • Distinguish between manual and automatic load shedding

title: 387-03-UKEU Economic Power System Operations
field_courseInformation: Stability of the Bulk Electric System relies heavily on the system operator's ability to maintain a balance of efficient and economic power production, transmission, and distribution. System operators must be familiar with the types of costs incurred on a system, how to efficiently load available generation types, how to manage transmission losses, and when exchanging power across borders is ideal. The Economic Power System Operations training course describes the system conditions contributing to or negatively impacting stable operations and inefficient generation unit loading. This online course is part of the System Operations training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the differences between fixed and variable costs
  • Explain the efficient operation of modern generating units
  • Describe economic generator loading
  • Assess the effects of varying fuel costs
  • Identify economic factors associated with the following types of generation: Nuclear, Solar, and Wind
  • Explain losses on a transmission system
  • Describe the economic interchange of power

title: 588-06 BESS Data Management and Reporting
field_courseInformation: Effective data management is essential for reliable operation, safety oversight, and regulatory compliance in utility-scale battery energy storage systems. In this lesson, learners examine how BESS data is collected, validated, protected, and analyzed to support operational decision-making and fault detection. Real-world examples illustrate how performance, safety, and market data are interpreted and correlated to reveal developing risks and optimization opportunities. The lesson also explains how accurate, well-managed data enables compliant reporting and supports long-term asset performance in regulated utility environments.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define BESS data management and explain its role in operational reliability and compliance
  • Identify key types of data collected in BESS operations, including performance, safety, and market participation data
  • Explain methods for ensuring data integrity, security, and accessibility
  • Recall best practices for analyzing BESS data to support fault detection, performance optimization, and decision-making
  • Describe how to generate regulatory-compliant reports for NERC, FERC, and ISO/RTO requirements
  • Identify the role of emerging technologies (AI, cloud platforms, blockchain) in improving BESS data management and reporting

The lesson also explains how emerging technologies and regulatory requirements influence daily operation, maintenance decisions, and long-term asset performance for battery installations.

• Define Battery Monitoring and Control (BMC) systems and their role in ensuring safe and reliable battery operation
  • Identify key parameters monitored by Battery Monitoring and Control (BMC) systems, including State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH), voltage, current, and temperature
  • Explain control strategies used to optimize charging, discharging, and balancing functions
  • Recall best practices for diagnosing battery faults
  • Recall best practices for preventing thermal events
  • Describe how technological advancements such as AI-driven analytics and digital twins enhance Battery Monitoring and Control (BMC) performance
  • Identify compliance and regulatory requirements relevant to battery monitoring and safety standards

title: 350-10-UKEU Generator Protection
field_courseInformation: Generators are susceptible to a variety of faults which require different methods of detecting and clearing. Because of the complex nature of generator protection, the Generation Protection training course covers UK and EU standards which address the detection and clearing of faults in frequency, voltage, and composite systems. Generator Protection is part of the System Protection training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify common internal faults of generation units
  • Identify system protection coordination requirements under Grid Codes and EU Network Codes
  • Recall external system conditions affecting generators
  • Define Composite Protection Systems
  • Recall applications of Composite Protection Systems
  • Recall the purpose of UFLS programmes
  • Recall generator relay settings and loadability principles
  • Identify protective relay loadability schemes
  • Recall the role of System Integrity Protection Schemes (SIPS) and Special Protection Schemes (SPS) in the UK and Ireland

title: 301-09-UKEU Intro to Distribution Systems
field_courseInformation: Understanding basic power distribution fundamentals is key to a reliable bulk power system. Being familiar with terminology, system voltages, power plants, and substations is key to avoiding issues and events on the grid. The Introduction to Distribution Systems training course discusses basic electrical terminology and addresses Faraday's Law and concepts. It explains electrical load characteristics for the bulk electric system. It also describes bulk electrical power systems including power plants, substations, and electrical safety. This course is part of the Distribution Systems training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Describe basic terminology and fundamental concepts relating to electrical energy production and delivery in large power systems
  • Describe the characteristics associated with resistive, inductive, and capacitive electrical load and utilization.
  • Describe how the Real-time electrical power system generates, transports, distributes, and delivers electrical energy to consumers

title: Protecting Yourself in the Sun
field_courseInformation: Sun exposure is an often-overlooked workplace hazard that can cause both short- and long-term health risks. This course explains how UV radiation affects the body and how to reduce its dangers through awareness, PPE, and safe work habits. You’ll learn to apply prevention strategies that protect not only your comfort but also your long-term health and safety on the job.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify common hazards that could cause employees harm from exposure the sun (it's important to acknowledge that sun exposure doesn't always equal heat)
  • Assess the specific risks of UV exposure, caused by the sun, that employees and coworkers may face in the workplace, (ok to mention artificial sources of UV radiation e.g., welding, UV lamps - but the focus here is sun exposure, we can develop a separate lesson for protection from artificial sources), by understanding what UV rays are, the types of UV radiation, and their short- and long-term health effects.
  • Identify the various PPE employees should have available for sun exposure
  • Implement safe practices and strategies to avoid harmful sun exposure relevant to specific working conditions
field_courseOutline:
• UV Radiation Basics
  • Understanding Sun Exposure
  • PPE for Sun Exposure
  • Safe Practices and Strategies
  • Regulations and Best Practices

title: Harassment Prevention & Respectful Workplace - Canada
field_courseInformation: This training fulfills Connecticut's Sexual Harassment Prevention training requirement for managers. Participants will learn about the different types of harassment, the laws that protect employees, and the proactive measures to prevent and address harassment in the workplace. By the end of this training, participants will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to contribute to a positive and inclusive work environment.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define Harassment: Define harassment accurately across all settings, including remote, hybrid, and in-person environments. This includes identifying sexual harassment, discrimination, and other forms of inappropriate behavior, and distinguishing them from acceptable workplace conduct.
  • Recognize Harassment: Identify various behaviors and situations that may constitute harassment, including subtle forms of harassment and power dynamics that contribute to harassment in the workplace.
  • Respond to Harassment: Understand the organization's reporting procedures for harassment, including who to report to, the steps involved in making a report, and the protections available for individuals who report harassment in good faith
  • Prevent Harassment: Leverage strategies that promote respect and inclusivity, establish personal and professional boundaries, and guidance on effective communication to prevent misunderstandings and conflicts.
  • Evaluate leadership practices that promote accountability, pro-social behavior, and a culture of belonging
  • Gain an understanding of the rules and guidelines surrounding retaliation in the workplace. Learn about how the EEOC's regulations apply to you and your team and how to avoid retaliation claims.

title: 350-06 - UKEU - Transformer Protection
field_courseInformation: Transformers are integral to transporting electrical energy through power systems and can be found at almost every generation facility and transmission substation. Because transformers have an integral role, protection is necessary. Transformer protection can address multiple fault types. Each fault type can be protected against with various relaying methods. The Transformer Protection training course describes the basic construction and protection methods commonly used in transformer protection. This online course is part of the System Protection training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Recall the basic construction of a common power transformer
  • Identify the different types of transformer faults
  • Identify the different types of pressure protection
  • Recall the advantages and disadvantages of using fuses, circuit switchers, and circuit breakers for overcurrent protection
  • Recall how earth fault protection is able to distinguish between an internal and external fault
  • Recall the basic operation of differential protection
  • Identify the different methods used to manage inrush current
  • Identify the conditions required in order for reactor banks to perform similar to transformers
  • Recall how capacitor banks detect and protect against severe imbalance
  • Identify the limitations of differential protection with phase shifting transformers

title: 507-03N Generator Construction and Process Control (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: Generator construction in the power industry is based on several standard operational principles. Once in operation, the generator is placed on the electrical grid using process control loops and other methods of control. The Generator Construction and Process Control training course describes generator construction and explains some of the principles behind generator operation and process control. This course is part of the Generator and Auxiliary Systems and Control training series. ILA HSI_SOS_001_50703
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the difference between induction and synchronous types of three-phase generators
  • Recall the construction of a three-phase, two pole DC generator
  • Recall how a sinusoidal waveform illustrates the number of amps produced over a given time
  • Recall the operation of a synchroscope
  • Identify the parameters to be controlled when placing the generator on the electrical grid

title: 507-01N Generator and Auxiliary Systems Functions (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: The generator is a major component of modern generation stations. It converts the energy in fossil fuels to electricity. The Generator and Auxiliary Systems' Functions online training course focuses on the generator and its auxiliary systems' functions. It also explains maintaining a generator for efficient operation. This course includes generator functions, generator cooling techniques, auxiliary systems, rotor winding assembly, and shaft sealing systems. It is part of the Generator and Auxiliary Systems and Control series. ILA HSI_SOS_001_50701
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define real power, reactive power, and the power factor
  • Identify the function of the rotor
  • Recall the importance of cooling particularly during load pickup
  • List advantages of hydrogen cooling and identify auxiliary systems associated with its use

title: 350-07N - Pilot Protection (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: System protection monitors system parameters to identify abnormal and unacceptable conditions. If one of those conditions occurs, the system protection will take appropriate action to avoid any damage to the system. To ensure coordination between all the system elements when a fault occurs, time delays are employed. Pilot protection is used to avoid extended damage to the system by quickly identifying the fault, taking appropriate action, and bypassing the time delay. The Pilot Protection training course discusses the major forms of communication channels used by pilot protection. It also explores basic functions of the more common pilot protection schemes deployed in power system protection. Pilot Protection is part of the System Protection training series. ILA HSI_SOS_001_350-07
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Recall why pilot protection systems are needed
  • Identify the strengths and weaknesses of the major communications channels
  • Identify which communications mediums are capable of high bandwidth data transmission
  • Identify the differences between permissive, blocking, and direct transfer trip schemes
  • Recall how pilot protection both manipulates and makes use of time delays
  • Define the difference between overreaching and under-reaching schemes

title: 588-03 - Battery Performance and Degradation
field_courseInformation: Battery degradation is a critical issue for today’s energy storage systems, influencing both performance and long-term costs. In this course, learners examine the causes of battery wear and how operational and environmental factors affect service life. Practical methods such as data interpretation, system monitoring, and corrective action planning are used to reinforce knowledge and promote real-world application. This training is best suited for engineers, technicians, analysts, and managers responsible for maintaining and optimizing BESS assets in industrial and utility-scale environments.

  • Recall best practices for mitigating degradation, including optimizing charge cycles, and maintaining environmental conditions.

title: 375-18 Real Power Balancing Concepts (2.5 CEH)
field_courseInformation:
Understanding real power balancing is essential for maintaining the reliability and stability of the Bulk Electric System (BES). Real Power Balancing Concepts explores one of the two fundamental operating functions of the BES: ensuring electrical generation and demand remain in constant balance. 
Reliability in the power grid is determined by two key factors:
•	Adequacy – the availability of sufficient resources to meet demand 24/7
•	Security – the ability to withstand disturbances with minimal disruption
This course provides system operators, engineers, and power professionals with a comprehensive understanding of balancing concepts and their impact on reliability. Course topics include:
•	Load-resource balance and the Balancing Authority
•	The control continuum in a Balancing Authority
•	ACE and inadvertent interchange
Real Power Balancing Concepts is part of the Resource and Demand Balancing training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Recognize the operation of a Balancing Authority (BA) Area
  • Match the five levels of control with the actions and resources that provide them
  • Recall the operation of a generator governor
  • Identify the components of the Area Control Error (ACE) equation
  • Identify the balancing standards as they apply to the levels of control
  • Calculate Inadvertent Interchange given frequency, schedules, and tie flows
  • List balancing actions taken during abnormal and emergency operations

field_courseInformation: General industry employees may be exposed to lead during manufacturing and recycling processes, cleanup and renovation operations, or while performing facility and equipment maintenance and repair. Knowing how exposure occurs helps reduce the risk of lead poisoning. The Lead Awareness training course explains the risks associated with lead, where it might be encountered, and the negative health effective it can cause. title: 301-04-UKEU Distribution System Components and Application
field_courseInformation:
A distribution system's complexity seems overwhelming even to the most experienced personnel. This complexity comes from how the components can be modified and manipulated to convert energy into usable levels for consumers. Regardless of a component’s design, it fulfills the same function universally.

The Distribution System Components and Application training course introduces configuration fundamentals, identifies the most common components, and clarifies the role a substation fills in a power system.
This course is part of the Distribution Systems training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Recognise distribution system components
  • Identify the common configuration, function, and elements of a simple distribution system
  • Identify primary supply line applications
  • Recognise the relationship between transmission, sub-transmission, and primary distribution
  • Identify the role of the substation
  • Identify the considerations of branch lateral design
  • Recognise the differences in overhead and underground component configuration

title: Safe and Respectful Workplaces: Addressing Bullying and Violence
field_courseInformation: Creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace is essential for fostering collaboration and productivity. This course examines the impact of workplace bullying and violence, explores their warning signs, and provides effective prevention strategies. By understanding how we can identify bullying, the four types of workplace violence, how we can prevent and respond to both, and how we can build a respectful workplace culture, participants will be equipped to prevent bullying and violence from taking root and ensure a supportive work environment for all.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Analyze the impact of workplace bullying and violence on the individual and organization; both in person and remote, and related to harassment
  • Identify warning signs and behaviors associated with bullying and the four types of workplace violence
  • Evaluate response strategies for when bullying is recognized and how to support victims
  • Evaluate leadership practices that promote accountability, pro-social behavior, and a culture of belonging
  • Apply those prevention and response strategies for bullying and violence to foster a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace culture.
field_courseOutline:
• The Costs of Workplace Bullying
  • Signs of Bullying
  • Responding to Bullying
  • Bystanders and Bullying
  • Standing Against Bullying
  • A Leaders Role in Preventing Bullying
  • Ineffective Mediations
  • Workplace Violence
  • An Opportunity to Intervene
  • Everyone's Roles in Prevention
  • Policies that Work
  • A Culture of Safety and Belonging

field_courseInformation: Sometimes, the wholesale electricity market’s complexity can cause prices to vary significantly, especially with high demand or low supply. title: 320-04 Ancillary Services UPM (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: Ancillary Services are transmission system services that support the transmission system. These services move electricity from generating sources to ultimate consumers. They support the transmission system in times of system stress or in the event of a system blackout and restoration. The Ancillary Services training course identifies and describes the typical services an ISO provides. It explains the differences between cost-based and market-based Ancillary Services. It also discusses how generation impacts the power grid's frequency. This online course is part of the Power Markets training series.

  • Describe Cost-Based and Market-Based Ancillary Service
  • List those Ancillary Services that are cost and market based

title: 320-03 Near Term, Day Ahead, Hour Ahead, Real Time Power Supply UPM  (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: Day-Ahead Markets and Real-Time Markets are critical power market components. The Day-Ahead Market is an ISO-controlled market for trading services for the next 24 hours. Day-Ahead Markets allow loads to plan their generation coverage a day in advance. Generators know what equipment needs to be running to provide the generation they've scheduled. Real-Time Markets are hourly. They enable loads to access additional power as needed when demand is higher than anticipated. Generators sell excess generation they either didn't sell or didn't offer in the Day-Ahead Market. These two markets help the ISO ensure reliability across its system. The Near Term, Day Ahead, Hour Ahead, Real Time Power Supply training course builds on information provided in the previous course. It discusses how short-term and day-ahead capability is applied within the ISO's environment. It describes the benefits and characteristics of the Day-Ahead Market. It identifies hour-ahead processes and explains the difference between Day-Ahead Market and Real-Time Market pricing. This online training course is part of the Power Market training series.

• Describe how short-term and day-ahead capability is applied within an ISO environment

  • List the hour-ahead processes

title: 320-01 Market Concepts UPM (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: Through the years, wholesale quantities of electricity have been bought and sold in various ways. Electric power has been transacted between entities since they connected their systems early in the 20th century. The power markets operate in much the same way today. How much does it cost? The price is typically negotiated at a fixed $/MWh rate or at some pre-agreed upon rate, similar to the current generation cost. The seller exports the energy and the buyer imports it. The power is normally delivered in hourly blocks, which could be pre-scheduled hours, days, or months ahead. Many transactions still operate this way. However, with deregulation in the 1990s, generating companies became more prevalent. These generators began competing with each other to supply electric load. These new operating conditions allowed market-based pricing to become the rule. The Market Concepts training course discusses the sale and purchase of bulk power. It explains the difference between cost-based and market-based transactions. It also describes the sellers and buyers roles. This course is part of the Power Markets training series.

title: 312-11 Generators, Torque, Angle and Synchronizing EPP (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation:
A power plant generator consists of a rotating magnetic field on a rotor inside armature windings on the generator's stator. The turning electromagnetic rotor causes lines of flux to cut through the coils in the stator. Voltage is induced in these coils, with current flowing to any load connected to the terminal of the generator. In the generator, the magnetic fields of the rotor and stator rotate at the same speed. The angle between 
the rotor and stator is the torque angle. Torque is the rotational force applied to the rotor. The torque angle is the generator's rotor position with respect to the phasor. For a generator to provide power to the system which must be synchronized. Specific conditions must match between the generator and the system for synchronization to happen. The Generators, Torque Angle, and Synchronizing training course explores how generator components work together to create power. It discusses single- and three-phase systems. It discusses how torque angle impacts a generator's output. Finally, it explains the conditions necessary to synchronize a generator to the system. This course is part of the Electric Power Principles training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Given a set of data, determine the direction of the electromagnetic force on a coil
  • Identify the operating principles of the generator
  • Define a delta connection
  • Using Kirchoff's Current Law, calculate the current relationship for a delta-connected load
  • Given a set of data, calculate the total three-phase load
  • Identify the impact of the torque angle on generation
  • Recall the relationship between power factor and torque angle
  • Recall the role of the synchroscope

field_courseInformation: Addressing drug and alcohol abuse in the workplace is important for several reasons. This abuse impacts employee well-being and health, leading to potential long-term physical and mental health issues, and it poses significant risks to workplace safety and productivity, leading to absenteeism, decreased output, and increased workplace accidents. From impaired cognitive function to strained interpersonal relationships, the impact on the individual is vast. Abuse can lead to behavioral changes, performance issues, and numerous physical and psychological effects that can be severe. In this course, gain an understanding the different types of substances and learn the laws and regulations surrounding drug and alcohol use in the workplace.
field_courseLearningObjectives: • Gain an understanding the different types of substances and learn the laws and regulations surrounding drug and alcohol use in the workplace.

title: 122-02 Drug and Alcohol Awareness
field_courseInformation: Driving while impaired by any substance - alcohol or drugs, whether legal or illegal - is against the law in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Law enforcement officers are trained to observe drivers' behavior and identify impaired drivers. Even in states where marijuana use is legal, driving under influence of the drug is still illegal. The Drug and Alcohol Awareness training course explains the effects of drugs and alcohol. It explains the DOT required testing process and the result-based consequences. Drug and Alcohol Awareness is part of the Transportation series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the effects of drugs and alcohol
  • Recall the DOT required testing process
  • Identify result-based consequences resulting from testing

title: 122-01 Safe Driving Practices
field_courseInformation: Driving for work is one of the most common and serious job-related risks across industries. In this course, learners explore how trip planning, pre-trip vehicle inspections, defensive driving techniques, and situational awareness reduce crash risk when operating light- and medium-duty vehicles. Real-world examples, hazard scenarios, and practical guidance reinforce how to recognize fatigue, distracted driving, and hazardous weather conditions. The course supports employees who drive for work by strengthening decision-making skills and promoting shared responsibility for workplace safety. Safe Driving Practices is part of the Transportation training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify employer and employee responsibilities for safe operation of work vehicles under OSHArs General Duty Clause
  • Recognize fatigue-related driving risk and the role of trip planning in reducing that risk
  • Identify required elements of a pre-trip vehicle inspection and appropriate defect reporting actions
  • Distinguish between safe driving behaviors and distracted driving behaviors
  • Select appropriate hazard-control actions when encountering distracted drivers or hazardous weather conditions
  • Apply the principles of following distance and reaction time to hazardous driving conditions
  • Explain the purpose of situational awareness and the OODA model in supporting safe driving decisions

title: 150-03 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures
field_courseInformation: Although most spills are accidental, they happen too often. Preventing spills is the best way to protect our health and the environment from exposure to oil. Spill prevention, control, and countermeasures (SPCC) plans are written and implemented by oil storage facility owners and operators to help them prevent spills from their facilities. The Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures training course describes the use of these plans. It also discusses common practices for preventing, responding to, and reporting spills. Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures is part of the Environmental Awareness training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Outline SPCC (spill prevention, control, and countermeasures) regulation guidelines
  • Explain how common secondary containment is used to prevent spills
  • Describe spill response and reporting tactics and procedures
  • Discuss the importance of performing visual inspections and routine maintenance

title: 150-02 Stormwater Regulations and Pollution Prevention Plans
field_courseInformation: Stormwater runoff is generated when precipitation from rain and snowmelt flow over the ground or other surfaces such as paved streets, parking lots, and building rooftops, and does not immediately sink into the soil. As the runoff flows over the ground, it accumulates debris, chemicals, sediment, and other pollutants that could adversely affect water quality. The Stormwater Regulations and Pollution Prevention Plans training course describes ways stormwater runoff can impact the environment. It also discusses stormwater regulations and explain how to effectively develop a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP). This course is part of the Environmental Awareness training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify major industrial sources of stormwater discharges
  • Discuss stormwater regulations implemented by the NPDES (National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) and EPA (Environmental Protection Agency)
  • Identify the components of a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP)
  • Describe the steps to produce and maintain an SWPPP

title: 140-18 Dog Bite Prevention
field_courseInformation: For some jobs, like meter reader, interactions with dogs are common. These encounters usually happen without incident, but they can sometimes be a serious hazard to employees. Dogs of all types may be encountered on the job, and it is best to be prepared for the worst scenarios. The Dog Bite Prevention training course describes techniques for preventing a dog attack. It provides methods for minimizing the severity of the injury if the attack cannot be prevented. Dog Bite Prevention is part of the Qualified Electric Worker training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify common causes of dog bites
  • Explain how interactions between dogs and humans can trigger dog bites
  • Define diseases transmittable by dog bite
  • Identify actions to take to avoid interactions with dogs on customer property
  • Define tools used for preventing dog bites
  • Identify ways to determine if a dog is present on the property
  • Recall manger responsibilities for workers who may experience interactions with dogs

field_courseInformation: Enclosed spaces have many similarities to confined spaces. However, the term "enclosed spaces" is specific to the electric power generation, transmission, and distribution industry. Enclosed spaces provide environments which can contain hazardous atmospheres. Familiarity with regulations for working in enclosed spaces creates safer working conditions. The Enclosed Spaces training course identifies the conditions of an enclosed space and how to eliminate or reduce the hazards associated with working in it. Enclosed Spaces is part of the Qualified Electric Worker training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define enclosed space, vault, and vented vault
  • Identify examples of hazardous atmospheres in an enclosed space
  • Recall OSHA regulations for handling enclosed space entry

title: 101-03 - Respiratory Protection Program
field_courseInformation: Policies, programs, and procedures exist in the workplace to provide employees with a safe and healthful working environment. Companies ensure worker safety by using facilities and equipment with feasible safeguards built into their designs to protect workers' respiratory health. When effective engineering controls are not available or being initiated, personal respiratory protection must be used to protect personnel. The Respiratory Protective Program training course identifies respiratory hazards. It explains how to use personal respiratory equipment to prevent injury or illness from poor breathing conditions. Respiratory Protection Program is part of the Personal Protective Equipment training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• State the goal of a respiratory protection program
  • Identify key components and key terms related to a respiratory protection program
  • Distinguish the responsibilities of roles under a respiratory protection program
  • State the purpose and timing of respiratory protection medical evaluations
  • Describe the functional difference between Air Purifying Respirators and Atmosphere-Supplying Respirators
  • Apply qualitative and quantitative fit testing procedures
  • Inspect, maintain, and properly store respiratory protection equipment
  • Outline required topics to cover during employee respiratory protection program training
field_courseRegulations: • 29 CFR 1910.134(k)(1) through (6)

title: 101-02 Hearing and Noise Safety
field_courseInformation: Well established evidence shows that worker exposure to noise of sufficient intensity and duration can result in hearing damage. Noise-induced hearing loss rarely results from just one exposure. It progresses unnoticed over a period of years. The Hearing Noise and Safety training course identifies conditions that lead to hearing damage or loss. It shows how to use engineering controls and personal protective equipment to prevent such damage. Hearing and Noise Safety is part of the Personal Protective Equipment training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify employee responsibilities regarding wearing hearing protective devices
  • Discuss the identification of hazardous noise areas
  • Discuss workplace noise control methods that include engineering controls and personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Describe the proper use and maintenance of hearing protective devices
field_courseRegulations:

title: 101-01 Personal Protective Equipment
field_courseInformation: A personal protective program protects employees by ensuring personal protective equipment (PPE) is provided and used whenever workplace hazards deem it necessary. A personal protective program also requires all PPE be maintained in a sanitary and reliable condition. The Personal Protective Equipment training course describes employer and employee requirements for reducing risk and avoiding injury, illness, and death by properly selecting, using, and maintaining PPE. It discusses the types and use of PPE. Personal Protective Equipment is part of the Personal Protective Equipment training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the different responsibilities of the safety and health manager, supervisors, and employee regarding the use of personal protective equipment
  • Identify the components of a training program for the use of PPE
  • Distinguish the types of equipment necessary to protect employees when working in conditions affecting the workersr health and safety
  • Describe the hierarchy of controls as it relates to personal protective equipment
field_courseRegulations: • 29 CFR 1910.132(f)(1) The employer shall provide training to each employee who is required by this section to use PPE.   • Describe the safety requirements for using pressure regulators and needle valves
  • Safely test cylinders and connections for leaks

  • Meet the requirements prescribed in the gas cylinder inspection checklist

title: 113-01 Forklifts and Powered Industrial Trucks Safety
field_courseInformation: All company employees required to operate a powered industrial truck or forklift must be trained to operate the equipment. Almost 70,000 accidents occur each year resulting in more than 80 fatalities and 35,000 series injuries when operating forklifts and other motorized trucks. Safety practices and procedures must be follow to ensure personnel safety. The Forklifts and Powered Industrial Trucks Safety training course explains the safe practices and procedures for minimizing the hazards of operating forklifts and other powered industrial trucks in the workplace.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Explain employee certification requirements
  • Describe supervisor responsibilities

field_courseInformation: Responding quickly and correctly to a medical emergency greatly increases the victim's chances for survival. Effective bystander CPR and Heimlich Maneuver administration can double the survival rate. The First Aid Resuscitation: Choking, CPR, and AED training course demonstrates how to assist victims using appropriate first aid techniques, including the Heimlich Maneuver, CPR, and using an AED. This course is part of the First Aid training series.

title: 103-02 Bloodborne Pathogens
field_courseInformation: Bloodborne pathogens are disease-causing microorganisms found in human blood. Occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials may put the employee at risk of infection by these microorganisms. The Bloodborne Pathogens training course identifies the diseases commonly caused by contact with bloodborne pathogens. It also describes safety measures and strategies to protect you from exposure to bloodborne pathogens. Bloodborne Pathogens is part of the First Aid training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Define bloodborne pathogens and identify potentially infectious materials
  • List diseases commonly caused by bloodborne pathogens
  • Discuss safety measures and strategies to reduce exposure to bloodborne pathogens
  • Recognize that workplaces with occupational exposure must maintain an exposure control plan

title: 103-01 First Aid
field_courseInformation: First aid describes a number of procedures and techniques for treating minor injuries and illnesses and major medical emergencies. Minor injuries include cuts, scrapes, bruises, minor burns, and minor sprains. First aid may be required during major emergencies or accidents that could result in death. Applying first aid techniques to treat severe bleeding, heart attack, or choking can safe the victim's life. The First Aid training course describes common injuries that require first aid treatment and how to provide aid for these injuries. It identifies major emergencies requiring emergency personnel and how to provide initial treatment for such injuries. It explains the importance of adhering to the universal precautions taken to prevent the transmission of bloodborne pathogens and prevent infections. First Aid is part of the First Aid training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Describe and apply minor first aid treatments
  • Describe emergency medical treatment
  • Describe actions taken during a medical emergency including: bleeding, physical shock, choking, burns, heat exhaustion, and poisoning
  • Define bloodborne pathogens (BBP) and provide examples
  • Identify the transmission of HBV and HIV
  • Identify and apply universal precautions to prevent transmission of bloodborne pathogens
  • Identify personal protective measures to prevent BBP infections
field_courseRegulations: • 29 CFR 1910.151(a) and (b)

field_courseInformation: Opioid overdoses can occur anywhere, and immediate, informed action saves lives.   • Demonstrate how to safely administer naloxone using nasal spray and injection methods.

  • Perform compression-only CPR if needed until professional help arrives.

title: 104-02 Fire Extinguisher Safety
field_courseInformation: The proper use and handling of fire extinguishers can minimize the damage and threat of injury or death should a small fire ignite in the workplace. All employees must understand the types of fire extinguishers available in each work area. Fire extinguisher safety includes knowing which fires to fight, when to fight them, and what extinguishers and methods to use. The Fire Extinguisher Safety training course identifies the four fire fuel sources and the appropriate extinguisher to put out a small fire. It also demonstrates the safest procedures for extinguishing a fire in the workplace. It describes the maintenance, inspection, and documentation requirements for fire extinguishers. This course is part of the Fire Prevention training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Describe the principles of fire extinguisher operation
  • Classify fuels to determine the proper fire extinguisher to use in case of fire
  • Recall the safest method of extinguishing a fire in the workplace
  • Identify what actions constitute an inspection
  • List corrective actions for rechargeable and non-rechargeable fire extinguishers
  • Describe the record-keeping requirements for the different types of inspections and maintenance activities

title: 150-01 - Environmental Awareness
field_courseInformation: Our understanding of the natural world has come a long way. Maintaining a thriving livable planet has become everyone's responsibility. This responsibility is especially true for individuals employed in planning, managing, and implementing industrial processes. These processes include diverse activities such as construction, mining, refining, manufacturing, and power, food, and essential services production. Understanding how individual actions impact the environment is critical to achieving the necessary balance between harvesting earth's resources and protecting its ecosystem. The Environmental Awareness training course identifies ways awareness can reduce the environment impact of various processes and tasks. It also describes how to design and implement an environmental management system (EMS). It discuss the overall goals of waste minimization and pollution prevention programs. This course is part of the Environmental Awareness training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the primary reasons for developing an environmental policy
  • Discuss common situations in which your environmental awareness can positively impact water and air quality
  • Describe ways to protect the environment when handling solid and hazardous waste, petroleum products, and substances such as PCB and asbestos
  • Describe the stages involved in the development of an environmental management system
  • Discuss the purpose of the National Waste Minimization Program
  • Identify common benefits of waste minimization and pollution prevention programs

field_courseInformation: One of the biggest misconceptions of electrical safety is high voltage kills people. Current, not voltage, causes electrical shock. Electrical shock occurs when current flows through a person's body. System voltages as low as 30 VAC can supply enough current to shock or even kill. The Electrical Safety training course describes the flow of electric current and common hazards of electricity. It explains safety procedures that prevent injury, damage, and death from electrical hazards. This course is part of the Electrical Safety training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Describe the flow of electrical current using the terms amp and volt
  • Identify electrical hazards
  • Minimize electrical hazards
  • Follow safe practices regarding work with or near electrical sources and circuits
  • Apply safety procedures to portable electrical equipment
  • Adhere to safe practices regarding the handling and use of electrical plugs and cords

title: 130-04 Confined Space Procedures
field_courseInformation: Facilities can require a great deal of maintenance which often occurs inside confined spaces such as tanks, vessels, boilers, or ductwork. It also explains the difference between a non-permit required confined space and a permit required confined space. Confined Space Procedures is part of the Behavior Based Safety Training series.

title: 588-02 - Battery Energy Storage System Design
field_courseInformation: Battery energy storage systems, or BESS, are integral components of modern energy infrastructure, enabling efficient management and use of electrical energy across numerous applications. Design of a BESS directly impacts its performance, safety, cost, and ability to support broader energy goals.   • Recall critical regulatory standards governing the deployment and operation of BESS

title: 388-14 Generator Operations for Maintaining Network Voltage Schedules VAR (1 CEH)
field_courseInformation: The electric generator is the primary source of reactive power and a dynamic source of reactive power when its AVR is in service. The AVR is designed to maintain a constant voltage. When in service, it immediately increases or decreases the amount of reactive power on the transmission system in response to changing conditions. When a generator trips off-line, its cannot supply or absorb MVAR. This event also changes the MW flow on the transmission system, affecting the transmission line load. Transmission Operators must recognize generator voltage regulators that might have to operate on manual or when the generator reactive capabilities are limited. The Generation Operation for Maintaining Network Voltages training course ensures generators provide reactive support and voltage control within generating facility capabilities to protect reactive equipment and maintain reliable operation of the Interconnection. This online training course is part of the Active and Reactive Power training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Explain the impact to system voltage when a high voltage transmission line is either placed into or taken out of service.
  • Identify why the Generator Operator must operate each generator connected to the interconnected transmission system in the automatic voltage control mode
  • Unless exempted, recall why the Generator Operator shall maintain the generator voltage or Reactive Power schedule
  • Identify the responsibilities of the Generator Owner in regards to the tap settings on step-up transformers
  • Recall why a Generator Operator must keep the Transmission Operator continuously informed of all significant changes in generator voltage

title: 388-12 Voltage and Reactive Control VAR (1.5 CEH)
field_courseInformation: North American Interconnections operate at 60 cycles per second. The connection between the current and voltage cycles relates to the voltage control on the Interconnection. That connection is the phase angle in a power system, which is the angular separation between the current and voltage cycles. Power systems exhibit three characteristics: resistive, capacitive, and inductive. Understanding these three characteristics is important to understanding power flow and voltage control. The Voltage and Reactive Control training course explains how to monitor, control, and maintain voltage levels, reactive flows and reactive resources to protect equipment and reliably operate the Interconnection. It describes the impact to system voltage when a high voltage transmission line is placed in service or taken out of service. This online course is part of the Active and Reactive Power training series.
field_courseLearningObjectives:
• Identify the responsibilities associated with the Transmission Operator regarding voltage and Reactive Power Schedules
  • Recall how Transmission Operators use surge impedance loading of a transmission line to monitor system voltage
  • Identify which reactive resources are available to the Transmission Operator to help regulate voltage levels
  • Recall how a Transmission Operator directs the operation of reactive resources in Real-time to regulate transmission voltage and reactive flow as necessary
  • Explain the impact to system voltage when a high voltage transmission line is either placed into or taken out of service.
